questions.question: My loan is through Northwind Auto Finance. After I sell you the car, how soon is the loan paid off, and can I skip my next payment?
answer_facts: the payoff goes to the lender the same day, because Northwind Auto Finance is in the e-payoff network
keep making payments until the lender confirms the loan is paid off
questions.perfect_answer: Northwind Auto Finance is in our e-payoff network, so we send your payoff the same day. Don't skip the next payment: keep paying until the lender confirms the loan is closed. If an extra payment goes through, the lender refunds it to you.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The lender's name is the only link to the e-payoff network article; payment timing is in getting_paid, and the 'keep paying' rule in a third article linked from it. 'Northwind' alone appears in 16 articles, so only the full name identifies the lender.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: I paid off my car, but the title still shows the bank as lienholder. I'm in Texas. Do I need a paper lien release before I can sell it to you?
answer_facts: Texas uses electronic titles, so the lender sends the lien release to the state electronically
ask the lender for a lien release, or sign NW-LRL-1 so Northwind contacts the lender (this can add 1 to 2 weeks)
you can still get an offer and book an appointment while you wait
questions.perfect_answer: The lien still has to be released, but Texas uses electronic titles, so your lender sends the release to the state electronically; there's no paper release to bring. Ask the lender to release it, or sign NW-LRL-1 and we contact them (this can add 1 to 2 weeks). You can get an offer and book your appointment meanwhile.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: lien_still_on_title only says 'in states with electronic titles'; which states those are is in the linked article.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: I moved to North Carolina, but my car is still registered in Virginia and the registration ran out in September. Can I sell it at a North Carolina store?
answer_facts: renew the registration before the appointment, because in North Carolina it must be current on the day of the sale
get an emissions certificate from a North Carolina inspection station
questions.perfect_answer: Yes, after two steps. In North Carolina the registration must be current on the day of the sale, so renew it before your appointment. And a car registered in another state needs an emissions certificate from a North Carolina inspection station before a North Carolina store can buy it. Bring the Virginia registration.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The expired-registration article answers half and links to the out-of-state article, which holds the emissions rule; the question never mentions emissions.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: My ex is still on the title, and I changed my last name back after the divorce, so my ID doesn't match the title either. What do I need to sell the car?
answer_facts: your ex has to sign too, unless the divorce decree awards the car to you (then bring a certified copy of the decree)
bring the document that shows the name change, such as the divorce decree
sign the name change affidavit, form NW-NMC-1
questions.perfect_answer: Your ex has to sign as a co-owner, unless your divorce decree awards the car to you; then bring a certified copy and their signature isn't needed. For the name, bring the document that shows the change (the divorce decree) and sign the name change affidavit, NW-NMC-1, at the appointment.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: Two situations in one question; the divorce article links to the name-mismatch article, which has the form.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: My car doesn't run anymore and the loan is with Meridian Auto Loans. How do I get the car to you, and do I need a payoff letter?
answer_facts: cars that don't run can't use home pickup
select stores tow it to the store at no charge
no payoff letter is needed, because Meridian Auto Loans is in the e-payoff network
questions.perfect_answer: Home pickup isn't available for cars that don't run, but select stores tow your car to the store at no charge; your offer page shows which ones. Meridian Auto Loans is in our e-payoff network, so you don't need a payoff letter: we confirm the payoff with them at the appointment.

questions.question: My dad wants me to sell his car for him. Does he have to sign the power of attorney in front of a notary? We live in Virginia.
answer_facts: no notary is needed in Virginia (only Georgia requires one)
he can sign power of attorney form NW-POA-2 electronically
questions.perfect_answer: No. Since February 1, 2026 the power of attorney is form NW-POA-2, which he can sign electronically with no notary; only Georgia still requires a notary. The old notarized NW-POA-1 is retired.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: selling_for_someone_else__2022 matches the question best and is current, but still says to sign NW-POA-1 in front of a notary (known issue KI-1). The current rule is reached through NW-POA-1 → replaced_by → NW-POA-2.

questions.question: I moved from Texas to Georgia. My paid-off car is still registered in Texas, and I can't find the title. Whose rules apply for a duplicate, and how long will it take?
answer_facts: the duplicate rules of the state that issued the title (Texas) apply
Texas titles are electronic, so for the sale you usually don't need a printed duplicate
a printed Texas duplicate takes 5 to 7 business days online
questions.perfect_answer: Texas rules apply, because the duplicate rules of the state that issued the title apply. Texas uses electronic titles, so for a sale to us you usually don't need a printout: we transfer the electronic title at the appointment. If you want a printed duplicate, request it online; it takes 5 to 7 business days.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The state filter uses the customer's state (Georgia), so it removes the Texas article that answers the question; the graph can walk to it (out_of_state → lost_title → duplicate_title_texas), but neighbours pass the same filter.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: I got my offer on October 29 and booked my appointment for October 31. Can I move it to November 4 and keep the same offer?
answer_facts: no: rescheduling keeps the offer only if the new time is on or before the offer's expiration date
offers are valid for 5 days (or 250 miles), so this one expires before November 4
you can request a new offer, which may be higher or lower
questions.perfect_answer: Not with the same offer. Offers are valid for 5 days or 250 miles, so an offer from October 29 expires before November 4, and rescheduling keeps the offer only if the new time is on or before the expiration date. Keep October 31, or request a new offer for November 4; the new amount may be higher or lower.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The rescheduling rule and the validity period are in two articles that link to each other; the answer needs both and a date calculation.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: Someone texted me saying they're from Northwind and that I have to wire the money I owe before my appointment, because my loan is higher than your offer. Is that legit?
answer_facts: no: Northwind never asks for wire transfers
the difference (negative equity) is paid only in person at the appointment
by cashier's check or debit card
questions.perfect_answer: No, that's a scam: Northwind never asks for wire transfers, gift cards or crypto. If you owe more than the offer, you pay the difference only in person at the appointment, by cashier's check or debit card. Don't respond, and report the message through the Help Center.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The scam article links to the negative-equity article, which says how the real payment works.
questions.author: claude
